item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-939fd50b46b97b15","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Banco de México reported that inflation remained high and core inflation persistent in early 2023; it raised the policy rate to 11% in February 2023, while maintaining that monetary-policy actions had anchored expectations and supported orderly financial markets. It forecast 2023 GDP growth at 0.8–2.4%, with a central estimate of 1.6%.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Early-2023 conditions and forecasts; Banxico actions were institutionally independent rather than directly attributed to AMLO.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes monetary decisions to Banco de México's Governing Board, not directly to López Obrador.","limitations":["The report does not establish AMLO's personal direction of monetary policy.","Forecasts are not realized full-year outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1d8e95a8a24b4820","start_unit":8,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The government reorganized social policy around universal or progressively universal transfers, created or revised programs, replaced the Social Development Secretariat with the Welfare Secretariat, and delivered benefits directly through cards or cash without intermediaries. However, Coneval evaluations found unclear target populations, weak infrastructure and staffing, insufficient performance in most evaluated actions, and limited measurable impact.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.7","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Describes the AMLO administration, with implementation evidence principally from 2019–2021 and policy continuation into 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the policy design and reorganization to López Obrador's government.","limitations":["Much of the evidence predates 2023.","The article synthesizes secondary reporting and does not provide a complete 2023 audit."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1d8e95a8a24b4820","start_unit":10,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"Between 2020 and 2022, Mexican poverty fell from 43.9% to 36.3% and extreme poverty from 8.5% to 7.1%; the source attributes the change to higher minimum wages, federal social programs, and remittances. At the same time, lack of access to health services rose from 16.2% to 39.1% between 2018 and 2022, and educational lag increased from 19% to 19.4%.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.8","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Outcome evidence through 2022, relevant to the inherited and 2023 policy trajectory.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes part of the poverty reduction to federal programs, while also identifying wage policy and remittances as contributors.","limitations":["The source does not establish the relative causal contribution of each factor.","Outcomes stop before the end of 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1d8e95a8a24b4820","start_unit":11,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"By the end of 2023, the adult-pension program reportedly covered 11.8 million beneficiaries receiving 2,400 pesos monthly; the program's budget rose from 100 billion pesos in 2019 to a planned 465 billion pesos, while Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro had fewer beneficiaries than at launch despite higher payments.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Includes 2023 beneficiary and budget figures, with some 2024 comparisons.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes expansion of these programs to López Obrador's administration.","limitations":["Some figures are reported from secondary sources and include planned 2024 amounts.","The evidence does not independently verify service quality or exclusion rates."]},{"source_id":"SRC-43819fe98d670bb9","start_unit":74,"end_unit":76,"fact_summary":"On December 29, 2023, López Obrador inaugurated a centralized 40,000-square-meter medicine warehouse intended to deliver unavailable medicines to hospitals nationwide within 24–48 hours. AP reported continuing shortages, unfilled prescriptions rising from 1.5 million in 2019 to 22 million in 2021 and about 12.5 million in 2022, and expert concern that extreme centralization could increase logistical and supply risks.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.4","6B.5","6B.6","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly relevant to a 2023 policy response, with shortage statistics extending through 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The warehouse and centralized purchasing model are explicitly presented as López Obrador's solution; operational criticism is attributed to AP's reporting and interviewed experts.","limitations":["The article cannot establish whether the promised delivery times or national coverage were achieved after inauguration.","Some shortages predated López Obrador, while AP identifies centralized procurement as partly government-created."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3fc1fe3508c600b4","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"In May 2023, López Obrador met privately with Morena and allied senators, including presidential contenders, and reportedly told them that one of them would succeed him; contemporaneous reporting also described fast-track approval of 20 reforms and disputes over legislative procedure.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.8","8B.1","8B.2","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns political conduct and legislative events in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The meeting is directly attributed to López Obrador; procedural allegations concern the Senate majority and executive-aligned legislators.","limitations":["The succession statement is based on attendee testimony reported in a press synthesis.","The document contains mixed-quality news and opinion items; procedural claims are not independently adjudicated here."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3fc1fe3508c600b4","start_unit":23,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"Opinion and reporting in May 2023 accused López Obrador of using polarizing rhetoric, attacking critics, pressuring or undermining independent institutions, and protecting or evading questions about alleged conflicts involving his sons; other reporting described the Supreme Court as constraining executive initiatives such as military control of the National Guard and the electoral reform plan.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.4","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","7B.2","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Contemporaneous 2023 reporting, but much of the material is commentary or allegation rather than a final finding.","ruler_attribution":"The allegations are directed at López Obrador and his administration; judicial constraints are attributed to the Supreme Court.","limitations":["The source is a press synthesis containing editorials and columns; allegations about family conflicts and institutional pressure are not final legal findings.","No claim of personal enrichment is established by these units alone."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3fc1fe3508c600b4","start_unit":12,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"The federal government accelerated construction of the Maya Train, transferred planned operation and administration to the military, faced reporting of cave and ecosystem damage on Tramo 5 Sur, and had numerous legal disputes involving contractors and subcontractors.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Reports active 2023 implementation and disputes concerning a major AMLO project.","ruler_attribution":"The project and decision to place operations under the military are attributed to the federal government under López Obrador.","limitations":["Environmental and contractor allegations are reported claims, not final adjudications.","The source does not provide a complete cost-benefit or outcome evaluation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3fc1fe3508c600b4","start_unit":14,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"The press synthesis reported that real spending on Mexico's energy-transition strategy fell 43.2% in 2022; CFE had accumulated large subsidies, debt, and losses under the administration; and Pemex's first-quarter 2023 profit fell 54% year-on-year while sales fell 19%.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Includes 2022 fiscal data and first-quarter 2023 company results.","ruler_attribution":"The financial and budgetary trends are reported in relation to federal state-owned enterprises and AMLO administration policy.","limitations":["The synthesis includes journalistic reporting and does not independently audit the figures.","The effects cannot be attributed solely to presidential decisions or separated from global energy prices."]},{"source_id":"SRC-57361184a7547261","start_unit":82,"end_unit":92,"fact_summary":"After Hurricane Otis struck Acapulco in October 2023, at least 45 people were reported dead, about 220,000 homes damaged, and 47 people missing. López Obrador deployed more than 10,000 troops and 1,000 government workers and promised aid, but AP found that poor residents reported little assistance, shortages of food, water, gasoline, medicine, and communications, and slower recovery in poorer neighborhoods; he also accused critics of exaggerating casualties.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.8","6B.10","7B.1","7B.2","7B.10","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns crisis management during October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Troop deployment, aid promises, and public statements are directly attributed to López Obrador; reported distribution failures concern the federal response.","limitations":["The report describes the early aftermath and cannot assess the full reconstruction period.","The death and damage figures were still evolving."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3ca77838d2d9bd3a","start_unit":1,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"INEGI reported that in the fourth quarter of 2022 Mexico had 60.1 million economically active people, 58.3 million employed, and unemployment of 3.0%, down from 3.7% a year earlier; female labor-force participation rose from 44.7% to 46.2%.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Baseline labor-market evidence immediately preceding 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source reports national outcomes without attributing causation to López Obrador.","limitations":["The document is a statistical baseline and does not evaluate government policy.","The period ends in 2022, not 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3ca77838d2d9bd3a","start_unit":9,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"In late 2022, 55.1% of employed people were in informal employment, 30.4% were in critical employment conditions, and 56.9% of employed women in the informal-employment measure were informal; unemployment fell, but labor precarity remained substantial.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.3","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Baseline labor-quality evidence immediately preceding 2023.","ruler_attribution":"INEGI reports the indicators without assigning responsibility to López Obrador.","limitations":["The evidence is not a direct 2023 outcome.","It does not identify which policies caused the changes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2f8b405bc92b4aae","start_unit":3,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The Baker Institute forecast that in 2023 López Obrador would continue expanding military responsibilities, face pressure from major projects and social programs, and pursue policies that critics viewed as weakening electoral institutions, regulatory independence, health, education, and the investment climate; it also described continued USMCA and energy disputes.","question_ids":["2B.6","2B.8","3B.2","3B.4","4B.2","4B.4","4B.9","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"A January 2023 forecast and assessment of the expected year.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes the forecast policy direction to López Obrador and Morena.","limitations":["This is a forecast, not a retrospective factual account of all 2023 outcomes.","The institute's assessments include interpretation and prediction."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2f8b405bc92b4aae","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The report stated that the administration's 2023 spending increases prioritized infrastructure and cash transfers, while programs lacked clear operating rules or accountability mechanisms; it also forecast fiscal pressure, borrowing, subsidies to PEMEX and CFE, and continued respect for Banxico autonomy.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2023 budget forecast and policy assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The spending and policy choices are attributed to the López Obrador government.","limitations":["The unit is predictive and does not verify executed spending.","Claims about missing accountability mechanisms are the report's assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2f8b405bc92b4aae","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"The report described low health spending, declining or inadequate health infrastructure, severe reductions in Insabi medical visits, and a proposed 2023 budget that would reduce resources for institutions serving people without federal coverage; it also described expected education learning losses and limited federal recovery action.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2020–2022 evidence and 2023 budget/outlook.","ruler_attribution":"The report links the institutional changes and budget choices to the López Obrador administration.","limitations":["Some evidence predates 2023 and some statements are forecasts.","The source does not provide a full 2023 service-delivery audit."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2f8b405bc92b4aae","start_unit":10,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"The report forecast continued high violence, militarized policing, organized-crime influence in elections and licit markets, persistent femicide, energy self-sufficiency failures, and a continued pragmatic but strained relationship with the United States; it concluded that governance institutions and human rights would likely weaken in 2023.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.5","2B.6","2B.8","2B.10","3B.2","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","4B.2","4B.4","4B.10","8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Forecast for 2023, including expected security, energy, and institutional developments.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the anticipated militarization, institutional weakening, and policy direction to López Obrador's administration.","limitations":["This is primarily a forecast rather than verified 2023 evidence.","Crime and violence outcomes are affected by organized criminal actors and other external constraints."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-8b9c01e558846323","SRC-5adda876afcd26e8","SRC-fd5c6e7225849846","SRC-e08f049fc55e44e9","SRC-0e8e8d7d5bece73d"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied documents are forecasts, metadata, historical legal archives, or later/current webpages rather than direct 2023 evaluations.","The supplied AP Otis article provides early crisis-response evidence but not the full subsequent reconstruction record.","Press-synthesis items include editorials and allegations that are material as reported claims but are not equivalent to final legal or audit findings."]}
